abstract: Centromere protein A (CENP-A), a centromeric histone H3 variant highly expressed in aggressive cancers, promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), yet its underlying mechanisms remain unresolved. Here, we used a reversible high-CENP-A expression system in human cells to follow EMT-state trajectories and CENP-A localization over time. Sustained CENP-A elevation shifted hybrid populations toward mesenchymal states and increased both centromeric loading and ectopic chromatin incorporation. Chromatin immunoprecipitation revealed ectopic CENP-A enrichment at EMT-associated loci. Single-nucleus multi-omics further resolved two EMT programs engaged at distinct cell cycle stages: CENP-A strengthened a pre-existing inflammatory program and triggered a developmental program. Importantly, restoring basal CENP-A levels erased these transcriptional programs and eliminated ectopic incorporation, consistent with a reversible, non-genetic mechanism. Together, our findings uncover a non-centromeric function for CENP-A in shaping epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity and cellular heterogeneity.
